content: 1. Sulfamethoxazole reduces the efficacy of the live typhoid vaccine through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Its use is contraindicated. 2. Trimethoprim also reduces the efficacy of the live typhoid vaccine via pharmacodynamic antagonism. Its use is contraindicated. Administration of live bacterial vaccines should be delayed until antibiotic therapy is completed. 3. Both trimethoprim and aliskiren increase serum potassium levels. Caution is advised, and monitoring is recommended. 4. Trimethoprim decreases urinary potassium excretion, which may lead to hyperkalemia, especially at high doses, in patients with renal insufficiency, or when combined with other hyperkalemia-inducing drugs. 5. Alpelisib reduces the levels or effects of trimethoprim by altering hepatic enzyme CYP2C9/10 metabolism. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is required. 6. Trimethoprim increases amantadine levels by reducing its elimination. Caution is advised, and monitoring is recommended. 7. Sulfamethoxazole also increases amantadine levels by reducing its elimination. Co-administration may impair renal clearance of amantadine, leading to elevated plasma concentrations. Caution and monitoring are advised. 8. Both trimethoprim and amiloride increase serum potassium levels. Caution is advised, and monitoring is recommended. 9. Amiodarone increases the levels or effects of sulfamethoxazole and trimethoprim by competing for renal tubular clearance as basic (cationic) drugs. Caution and monitoring are advised. 10. Amitriptyline and sulfamethoxazole both prolong the QTc interval. Similarly, amitriptyline and trimethoprim both prolong the QTc interval. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is required. 11. Amoxapine and trimethoprim, as well as amoxapine and sulfamethoxazole, both prolong the QTc interval. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is required. 12. Apalutamide reduces the levels or effects of trimethoprim by inducing hepatic enzyme CYP2C9/10 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. Co-administration with CYP2C9 substrates may result in reduced exposure to these medications, necessitating evaluation for therapeutic efficacy. 13. Sulfamethoxazole and artemether/lumefantrine both prolong the QTc interval. Similarly, artemether/lumefantrine and trimethoprim both prolong the QTc interval. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is required. 14. Aspirin and sulfamethoxazole may increase each other's effects through competition for plasma protein binding. The risk is low with low-dose aspirin. Caution and monitoring are advised. 15. Sulfamethoxazole reduces the levels or effects of bazedoxifene/conjugated estrogens by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of the hormone and carries a low risk of contraceptive failure. Caution and monitoring are advised. 16. Trimethoprim and benazepril both increase serum potassium levels. Caution is advised, and monitoring is recommended. 17. Sulfamethoxazole increases the levels or effects of carvedilol by altering hepatic enzyme CYP2C9/10 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 18. Trimethoprim and canagliflozin both increase serum potassium levels. Caution is advised, and monitoring is recommended. 19. Trimethoprim and candesartan both increase serum potassium levels. Caution is advised, and monitoring is recommended. 20. Cannabidiol increases the levels or effects of trimethoprim by inhibiting metabolism, potentially through CYP2C9 inhibition. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is required. Dose reduction may be necessary when using CYP2C9 substrates concurrently. 21. Trimethoprim and captopril both increase serum potassium levels. Caution is advised, and monitoring is recommended. 22. Chlorpromazine and sulfamethoxazole both prolong the QTc interval. Similarly, chlorpromazine and trimethoprim both prolong the QTc interval. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is required. 23. Cimetidine increases the levels or effects of trimethoprim and sulfamethoxazole by competing for renal tubular clearance as basic (cationic) drugs. Caution and monitoring are advised. 24. Clarithromycin and trimethoprim, as well as clarithromycin and sulfamethoxazole, both prolong the QTc interval. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is required. 25. Clomipramine and sulfamethoxazole both prolong the QTc interval. Similarly, clomipramine and trimethoprim both prolong the QTc interval. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is required. 26. Trimethoprim reduces the levels or effects of conjugated estrogens by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of the hormone and carries a low risk of contraceptive failure. Caution and monitoring are advised. 27. Crofelemer increases trimethoprim levels by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. Crofelemer is unlikely to inhibit systemically due to minimal absorption. 28. Sulfamethoxazole and cyclosporine may increase each other's nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity. Caution and monitoring are advised. 29. Trimethoprim and cyclosporine both increase serum potassium levels. Caution is advised, and monitoring is recommended. 30. Dabrafenib reduces the levels or effects of trimethoprim by altering hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is required. 31. Trimethoprim increases the toxicity of topical dapsone by reducing its metabolism, leading to increased systemic exposure of dapsone and its metabolites. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is required. 32. Sulfamethoxazole increases the toxicity of topical dapsone by reducing its metabolism, potentially inducing methemoglobinemia. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is required. 33. Desipramine and sulfamethoxazole both prolong the QTc interval. Similarly, desipramine and trimethoprim both prolong the QTc interval. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is required. 34. Digoxin levels or effects are increased by trimethoprim and sulfamethoxazole through competition for renal tubular clearance as basic (cationic) drugs. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. Caution and monitoring are advised. 35. Dofetilide and trimethoprim both prolong the QTc interval. Sulfamethoxazole increases the levels or effects of dofetilide through competition for renal tubular clearance. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is required. 36. Sulfamethoxazole and dolasetron both prolong the QTc interval. Similarly, dolasetron and trimethoprim both prolong the QTc interval. Caution and monitoring are advised. 37. Doxepin and trimethoprim, as well as doxepin and sulfamethoxazole, both prolong the QTc interval. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is required. 38. Sulfamethoxazole increases the levels or effects of dronabinol by altering hepatic enzyme CYP2C9/10 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 39. Dronedarone and trimethoprim both prolong the QTc interval. Similarly, sulfamethoxazole and dronedarone both prolong the QTc interval. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is required. 40. Droperidol and trimethoprim, as well as sulfamethoxazole and droperidol, both prolong the QTc interval. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is required. 41. Efavirenz increases the levels or effects of sulfamethoxazole by altering hepatic enzyme CYP2C9/10 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 42. Elagolix reduces trimethoprim levels by inducing hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is required. 43. Sulfamethoxazole increases the levels or effects of eltrombopag by altering hepatic enzyme CYP2C9/10 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 44. Sulfamethoxazole increases eluxadoline levels by altering hepatic enzyme CYP2C9/10 metabolism. Caution is advised due to incomplete information on eluxadoline metabolism. 45. Elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF increases trimethoprim levels by altering hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is required. 46. Trimethoprim and enalapril both increase serum potassium levels. Caution is advised, and monitoring is recommended. 47. Encorafenib affects trimethoprim metabolism by inhibiting and inducing CYP3A4. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is required. 48. Epinephrine and trimethoprim, as well as epinephrine and sulfamethoxazole, both prolong the QTc interval. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is required. 49. Trimethoprim and eplerenone both increase serum potassium levels. Caution is advised, and monitoring is recommended. 50. Sulfamethoxazole and erythromycin base both prolong the QTc interval. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is required. 51. Trimethoprim and eprosartan both increase serum potassium levels. Caution is advised, and monitoring is recommended. 52. Erdafitinib increases trimethoprim levels by reducing renal clearance. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is required. 53. Sulfamethoxazole and erythromycin ethylsuccinate both prolong the QTc interval. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is required. 54. Trimethoprim reduces estradiol levels by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of the hormone and carries a low risk of contraceptive failure. Caution and monitoring are advised. 55. Sulfamethoxazole reduces estradiol levels by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of the hormone and carries a low risk of contraceptive failure. Caution and monitoring are advised. 56. Sulfamethoxazole increases the levels or effects of ethosuximide by altering hepatic enzyme CYP2C9/10 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 57. Fedratinib increases trimethoprim levels by altering hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is required.
